rules.description: High-autonomy agent request touching privileged tools or sensitive environments.
rules.impact: A highly capable agent can chain small permissions into large operational impact without further review.
rules.recommendation: Deny autonomous execution until sandboxing, network egress controls, workspace boundaries, and approval gates are verified.

rules.description: MCP/tool manifest exposes sensitive or high-impact capabilities.
rules.impact: A poisoned or over-permissive connector can convert untrusted text into unauthorized tool use.
rules.recommendation: Review connector permissions, remove unnecessary scopes, and require trust verification before enabling the tool.

rules.pattern: \b(network|internet|egress|webhook|external url|remote server|public endpoint)\b.{0,180}\b(allow all|unrestricted|no approval|default allow|wildcard)\b
rules.description: Network or egress policy appears overly permissive.
rules.impact: Unrestricted outbound access can let a compromised agent leak data or call attacker-controlled services.
rules.recommendation: Use network deny-by-default, destination allowlists, and separate approval for external requests.

rules.pattern: \b(always approve|approve all|remember my approval|do not ask again|skip confirmation|reduce prompts)\b
rules.description: Request may weaken human approval gates or create approval fatigue.
rules.impact: Repeated or blanket approvals reduce meaningful supervision and can normalize unsafe actions.
rules.recommendation: Keep fail-closed defaults, batch low-risk approvals carefully, and require fresh approval for high-impact tools.
